properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 22 at 11:09AM MST until October 22 at 11:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 1109 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles northeast
of Aripine, or 15 miles northeast of Heber-Overgaard, moving
northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Navajo County.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 377 between mile markers 7 and 8. State Route 277 between
mile markers 317 and 328.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing large hail.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 800 PM MST Thursday for a
portion of north central Arizona.

NWSheadline: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1115 AM MST FOR NAVAJO COUNTY

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:40AM MDT until October 22 at 3:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 345 PM MDT.

* At 1140 AM MDT, Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen across
the headwaters of Gould Wash from earlier thunderstorms which
created a large flood wave which continues to move through
Hurricane. Additional thunderstorms forming to the south and west
are expected to move back into this area exacerbating the flooding
within the next 30 to 45 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gould Wash through Hurricane.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:45 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:45 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend. There
is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage next week,
after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet Roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:13AM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and river flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected, especially along the San
Juan River down to the Navajo River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1107 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected in the warned area.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over the last 24
hours. Excess runoff from rainfall will cause the San Juan River
to rise downstream to the Navajo River, potentially inundating
homes.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River, Blanco, Rio, Montezuma Creek and Navajo River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Juanita and Gato.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM MDT FRIDAY

properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 22 at 9:30AM MST until October 22 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
TORFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 1000 AM MST.

* At 930 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Village of Oak Creek, or 6 miles south of Sedona,
moving north at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Sedona and Red Rock State Park.

This includes State Route 89A between mile markers 365 and 371.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Crescent Moon Ranch.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

CMAMtext: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 10:00 AM MST. Take shelter now. Check media.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 10:00 AM MST. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying debris. Check media.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:54AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest New Mexico, including the following
areas, Central Grant County/Silver City Area, Eastern Black Range
Foothills, Southern Gila Foothills/Mimbres Valley, Southern Gila
Region Highlands/Black Range, Southwest Desert/Lower Gila River
Valley and Upper Gila River Valley.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An incoming potent upper level system coupled with abnormally
high moisture will allow for scattered to numerous thunderstorms
this afternoon, evening and into Friday morning. Storms will be
efficient rain makers which could lead to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 12:04PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 1204 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Quail Creek State Park, or 21 miles southwest of Zion National Park,
moving north at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Hurricane, New Harmony, Quail Creek State Park, Toquerville, Leeds
and Pine Valley.

This includes Interstate 15 between mile markers 16 and 30.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT CENTRAL WASHINGTON COUNTY UNTIL 1230 PM MDT
